new_compositional_issues: G0 (external state rollback) and G3 (global rollback) execution sequence is not strictly automated as a unified flow. If G3 restores files before G0 tears down external state, local references to external state could mismatch, though relying on the T-1 backup inventory mitigates this.
The added complexity of 31 specs increases execution context length drastically. This may cause the executing LLM to hallucinate or truncate steps mid-wave due to context window exhaustion.
regressions_from_fixes_integration: The rigid G1 inter-wave gates enforce strict MCP reachability (e.g., nuzantara-rag.fly.dev/health). If the external service has a temporary network hiccup, the entire wave execution pipeline will hard-block, requiring manual override.
Manual teardown for Vercel and Fly in G0 breaks the absolute 'single-command rollback' promise of G3, leaving a minor footprint of irreversible cloud state.
still_missing: Automated sandbox testing for the G0 and G3 rollback scripts before they are relied upon in production.
A mechanism to safely pause/quiesce Claude processes during the T-1 backup phase (similar to the pkill in G3) to ensure the initial tarball doesn't capture a torn SQLite transaction.
honest_admission: In my first pass, I focused heavily on architectural orchestration and state tracking (T-2, G0), but I completely missed the low-level SQLite WAL/SHM corruption vector during file backup. I also overlooked the guardrail bypasses (SQL/MultiEdit) in T1.2 and the password leak in T3.2. GPT-5.5's lower-level, adversarial code review caught critical operational and security bugs that I skimmed over.
